theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: The press brake operator at a fabrication shop in Spanish Town calls you to a breakdown. What should you do first when you arrive?
options: Take the side cover off to look inside
Make the area safe and hear what the operator saw
Restart the machine to hear the fault
Order a new motor now, in case it turns out to be needed

questions.stem: Why should you ask the operator exactly what happened just before the machine stopped?
options: It gives clues to the cause and saves time
So the operator can be blamed in the report
So you do not need to look at the machine
It is needed only for the insurance claim

questions.stem: A conveyor in a steel stockyard has stopped with a jam. A worker reaches in to clear it while the motor is stopped only at the stop button. What should the team leader do?
options: Let him carry on, as the motor has already stopped
Stand at the stop button while he works
Stop him: it must be isolated and locked first
Turn the conveyor slowly by hand to help him

questions.stem: A factory uses a permit-to-work system for its plant. Who may carry out breakdown work on a machine there?
options: Any worker who knows the machine well
The operator, as long as a fitter is nearby
Anyone who has the right tools for the job
Only authorised people named on the permit

questions.stem: Which set of details is normally written on a permit to work for a machine breakdown?
options: The job, hazards, isolations and who may work
The machine's price and the maker's address
The names of everyone in the factory
The operator's wages and hours for the week

questions.stem: What is the right order for making a machine safe before breakdown work?
options: Remove the guards, then switch off at the panel
Stop it, isolate, lock and tag, then prove it is safe
Tag it, start the repair, then lock it off later when free
Switch off at the stop button, then start work

questions.stem: Why does each person working on a machine fit his or her own padlock to the isolator, using a multi-lock hasp?
options: So the machine looks safe to the manager
So the keys can be shared round the team
So no one can switch on while anyone is at work
So the team leader can remove all the locks

questions.stem: After locking off a machine, how is it proved that it cannot start?
options: Look at the isolator handle and trust that it is really off
With all clear, try the start, then set it back to off
Ask the operator if he thinks it is off
Listen for the motor to stop humming

questions.stem: During a breakdown you find burnt wires inside a machine's control panel. You are the fabrication fitter on the job. What should you do?
options: Leave it for the licensed electrician under the permit
Cut out the burnt part and join the new wires yourself
Tape the wires and restart the machine
Swap the fuse for a bigger one

questions.stem: A hydraulic press has been isolated and locked off at the electrical supply. Why may it still be unsafe to put hands under the ram?
options: The oil may be too cold to work
The press may still be under its warranty
Hydraulic pressure or the ram's weight can still move it
The warning lights on the control panel may still be lit up

questions.stem: How should the raised ram or top beam of a press be made safe before anyone works under it?
options: Hold it up by keeping the pump running
Ask a worker to watch it and shout if it moves
Prop it up with any piece of timber found in the yard
Lower it, or block it with the maker's safety blocks

questions.stem: A fitter must take off a hose from a pneumatic clamp on a welding jig. What must be done first?
options: Isolate the air and bleed the line to zero
Pull the hose off quickly to stop it whipping
Wrap the hose in a rag and loosen it slowly
Turn the compressor up so the clamp holds

questions.stem: A guillotine shear has been switched off at the isolator. Which hazard may still be there?
options: The shop lights may go out
A heavy flywheel may still be turning
The blade may have rusted overnight
The motor may have cooled down

questions.stem: Why is a logical fault-finding method better than changing parts until the machine works?
options: It always needs fewer tools
It means no report has to be written
It finds the real cause quickly, without waste
It lets the operator do the whole repair on his own

questions.stem: A bearing on a plate roll bender is running hot and noisy. Which cause is most likely?
options: Too much paint on the rolls
The shop is too brightly lit
The plate being rolled is too short
Lack of grease, or a worn bearing

questions.stem: Why should the fitter read the machine's maintenance history before stripping it down?
options: Repeat faults point towards the real cause
It shows how much the machine first cost
It tells you who to blame for the fault
The history must be signed before any work

questions.stem: Where should you find the correct tightening torques and fitting order for a machine's parts?
options: From what the operator remembers
In the maker's service manual
On the shop's notice board
From another machine of a different make

questions.stem: The V-belts on a pedestal drill's drive squeal and slip when drilling. What is the most likely cause?
options: The drill bit is too sharp
The belts are loose or worn
The motor runs too fast
The table is set too low

questions.stem: The drive chain on a powered roller conveyor keeps jumping off its sprocket. What should be checked?
options: The colour of the chain paint
Only the speed of the motor
The load on the far end of the conveyor
Sprocket line-up, chain wear and tension

questions.stem: The cast iron gearbox housing of a section bender has cracked. Production wants it welded at once. What should the Level 3 fitter recommend?
options: Weld it at once with any steel electrode
Glue the crack and run the machine slowly
Replace it, or repair it to an approved procedure
Leave it cracked and run it until it breaks right through

questions.stem: When is a temporary repair acceptable during a breakdown?
options: When it is safe, approved, recorded and replaced later
Whenever production has fallen behind its target for the day
Only if the operator agrees to it
Whenever the right spare is too dear

questions.stem: A broken guard bracket on a conveyor must be welded in place. Why is the earth (return) clamp fixed close to the weld, on the same part?
options: So the clamp does not get lost in the machine
So the arc starts more easily
So weld current cannot pass through bearings
So the weld cools down faster

questions.stem: A machine fitted with electronic controls needs a weld repair on its frame. What should be done before welding?
options: Nothing, as the machine is switched off
Follow the maker's advice to protect the controls
Earth the welder to the control panel
Run the machine while welding so that it stays cool

questions.stem: A breakdown repair needs welding close to the hydraulic hoses of a press. Which control matters most?
options: Shield or remove the hoses, and keep a fire watch
Turn up the pump so that the oil stays cool and safe
Weld faster so the hoses do not get hot
Spray water on the hoses while welding

questions.stem: Besides the isolation, which extra permit is usually needed before welding or grinding during a breakdown in a factory?
options: A driving permit
A building permit
A food handler's permit
A hot work permit

questions.stem: The right replacement bearing is not in stores. A fitter offers one that 'nearly fits'. What should the team leader do?
options: Fit it, and pack the gap with shim
Fit it until someone complains
Use only the right part, or one approved as equal
Fit it, and leave the old one beside the machine as a spare

questions.stem: Why should the part number be read from the old part or the parts list before a new one is ordered?
options: To get the exact size and type
So the supplier can set a price
So the old part can be sold
To find the maker's phone number

questions.stem: Why should parts be laid out in order, and marked, as a machine is stripped down?
options: So they can be counted for stores
So it goes back together correctly
So the machine looks tidy in photos
So the parts dry out faster

questions.stem: Why must the guards be refitted before a repaired machine is test run?
options: The test run has the same hazards as normal use
Guards make the machine run more quietly
Guards help the machine reach full speed
The guards are needed only for the record photos

questions.stem: At the end of the job, who should take a personal padlock off the isolator?
options: The machine operator
Any member of the team
Only the person who fitted it
The first person to finish

questions.stem: What must happen before a repaired machine is handed back to production?
options: The operator just presses start
The fitter leaves a note on the door
The guards are left off for a day
Test run, checks, then the permit signed off

questions.stem: During the test run, a repaired roll bender makes a new knocking noise. What should you do?
options: Stop, isolate it again, and find the cause
Turn the radio up so the noise is not heard
Hand it over and see if the noise stops
Add more grease while it runs

questions.stem: After a new gearbox is fitted, why are the oil level and grade checked against the maker's data?
options: So the oil matches the paint
So the oil lasts for ever
Wrong oil or level can wreck the gears
So the gearbox runs faster than before

questions.stem: Why is shaft alignment checked after a motor and a pump are refitted on the shop's water-cooling system?
options: To make the pump look straight
Misalignment wears bearings and couplings early
So the motor runs on less power at once
So the guard is easier to fit

questions.stem: Which set of information belongs in a breakdown report?
options: The fault, cause, work done, parts and downtime
Only the time the fitter arrived
Only the name of the operator
The weather and the lunch times of the shift that day

questions.stem: Why should the cause of a breakdown be recorded, and not only the parts that were replaced?
options: So the report is longer
So the same failure can be prevented
So the operator can be disciplined
So the parts can be returned

questions.stem: The same bolt on a shear's blade holder has broken three times in one month. What should the team leader do?
options: Fit a stronger bolt each time without telling anyone
Keep a box of spare bolts by the machine
Find the root cause, not just fit another bolt
Tell the operator to use the shear less often

questions.stem: A production line loses J$45 000 of output for every hour it is stopped. A breakdown lasts 3 hours 20 minutes. What is the value of the lost output?
A plasma cutting table broke down 4 times in 1 200 running hours. What is the average running time between breakdowns?
options: 30 hours
300 hours
400 hours
4 800 hours

questions.stem: A spare drive belt is used 3 times a month. A new order takes 2 months to arrive. What is the least number to keep in stores so they do not run out while waiting?
You lead a breakdown team of three. The production supervisor asks you to skip the lock-off 'just this once' because it is a quick job. What should you do?
options: Agree, as it is only a quick job
Agree, if someone stands by the switch
Agree, but only for the most skilled fitter
Refuse, and isolate and lock off as normal

questions.stem: Why should the production supervisor be told the likely repair time as soon as it is known?
options: So production can plan round the downtime
So the fitters can take a longer lunch
So the report need not be written
So the supervisor can do the repair

questions.stem: What is the main difference between breakdown maintenance and planned (preventive) maintenance?
options: Planned work is always done only by the machine operator
Breakdown repairs need no permit
Breakdown work fixes failures; planned work stops them
Planned work is done only after a failure

questions.stem: A new trainee is helping on a breakdown. Which task is right for him while he learns?
options: Removing other people's locks at the end
Laying out and labelling parts under your eye
Signing off the permit for the team
Doing the electrical tests alone

questions.stem: At the end of a repair, oily rags, old grease and used oil are left by the machine. What is right?
options: Put them in the marked bins for safe disposal
Pour the oil down the yard drain
Burn the rags in the scrap skip
Leave them for the operator to clear

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What three-word name, often shortened to PTW, is given to the signed system that controls breakdown work on plant?
What do the letters LOTO stand for in machine safety?
Name the clip, with holes for many padlocks, that keeps an isolator locked until the last worker's lock is taken off.
What name is given to the energy left in a machine after it is isolated, such as in a raised ram, a spring or trapped air?
What is the name of the maker's book that gives the repair steps, settings and parts lists for a machine?
What tool is used to tighten a bolt to a set value in newton metres?
What one word means the time a machine is stopped and not producing?
A spanner 0.3 m long is pulled at its end with a force of 100 N. What torque is applied, in N·m?
What two-word term means finding the real, underlying reason a breakdown happened?
Which measuring instrument, with a needle on a round face, is used to check shaft run-out and alignment?
A line stopped at 9:40 a.m. and restarted at 1:15 p.m. on the same day. How many minutes of downtime was that?
What two-word name is given to a repair that keeps a machine running safely until a proper repair can be made?
What do the letters MTBF stand for in maintenance records?
What is the name of the device placed in a press to stop the ram or beam coming down while people work under it?
What is the name of the label hung on a locked isolator, showing who locked it, when and why?

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would follow from the moment you are called to a machine breakdown until you are ready to start work on it.
essays.modelAnswer: I go to the machine with my PPE and basic tools. First I make the area safe: I keep people back and check for oil leaks, hot parts, trapped material or anyone hurt. I ask the operator what happened, what the machine was doing, and any noises, smells or warnings before it stopped. I look at the machine from outside and note what I can see, without touching moving parts. I read the maintenance history and the maker's manual. Then I arrange a permit to work with the authorised person, listing the job and hazards. The machine is isolated from every energy source: electrical, hydraulic, air and stored energy. Each worker fits a personal lock and tag to the hasp, and the machine is proved safe by trying the start with everyone clear. Only then do I start work.
markingPoints: Makes the area safe and checks for injured people
Gets the operator's account and looks without touching
Checks history and maker's manual
Permit to work with an authorised person
Isolates all energy, personal locks and tags, proves safe

essays.stem: Explain how a fabrication shop machine that has electrical, hydraulic and air power is isolated and locked off, and how it is proved safe before work.
essays.modelAnswer: The machine is first stopped in the normal way by the operator. The authorised person, with the permit, then isolates each energy source. The electrical supply is switched off at the isolator, which is locked off with a hasp, and the licensed electrician proves it dead with a tester that is checked before and after use. The air supply valve is closed and locked, and the air is bled from the lines and the receiver on the machine. The hydraulic pump stops with the power, but the pressure is released as the maker says and any raised part is lowered or blocked. Each person fits a personal lock and a tag, showing name and date, to every isolation point. With everyone clear, the start control is tried to prove nothing moves, and then returned to off. The isolations are written on the permit.
markingPoints: Stops first; authorised person and permit
Electrical isolated, locked and proved dead by the electrician with a checked tester
Air isolated and bled
Hydraulic pressure released; raised parts lowered or blocked
Personal locks and tags; try start; record on permit

essays.stem: Explain what stored energy is, give four examples in a fabrication shop, and say how each one is made safe before breakdown work.
essays.modelAnswer: Stored energy is energy that stays in a machine after its supply is isolated, and can still make parts move, spring or spray. One example is a raised press brake beam or ram, which can fall under its own weight; it is lowered fully or held with the maker's safety blocks. A second is hydraulic pressure trapped in a cylinder or accumulator; it is released through the bleed valve as the maker says, and the gauge is checked at zero. A third is compressed air in a jig clamp or the line; the air is isolated and bled before any hose is opened. A fourth is a flywheel or blade still turning on a shear after it is switched off; you wait until it stops and check it is still. Springs under tension, such as on a clamp, are also released or held before parts are removed.
markingPoints: Clear definition of stored energy
Raised ram or beam: lowered or blocked
Hydraulic pressure: released, gauge at zero
Air pressure: isolated and bled
Flywheel or springs: wait to stop, release or restrain

essays.stem: Describe a logical method for finding the cause of a breakdown on a machine such as a roll bender or shear.
essays.modelAnswer: I start by collecting facts: what the operator saw and heard, when it happened, and what the machine was doing. I check the maintenance history for repeat faults. With the machine isolated, I look, listen and feel: for oil leaks, loose or broken parts, burnt smells, worn belts, hot bearings and damage. I use the maker's manual and drawings to understand how the drive works, and follow the power from the motor through belts, gears and shafts to the rolls or blade. I check the simple and likely causes first, such as a sheared key, a loose belt or a tripped overload, which the electrician checks. I split the system into parts and test each one to narrow the search. When I find the fault, I ask why it happened, so the root cause can be fixed and not only the broken part. I record what I found.
markingPoints: Collects facts from the operator and the history
Looks, listens and feels with the machine isolated
Uses the manual and follows the drive path
Checks simple causes first and narrows down step by step
Finds and records the root cause

essays.stem: A broken bracket must be welded on a conveyor during a breakdown. Explain how you would plan and carry out the weld safely without harming the machine.
essays.modelAnswer: I make sure the conveyor is isolated and locked off under a permit, and I get a hot work permit. I check what is near: belts, hydraulic or grease lines, plastic covers, cables and anything that can burn, and I remove or shield them with welding blankets. I clean the broken area and check what steel it is, so I can choose the right electrode and procedure. If the bracket is a load-bearing part, I check the repair is approved. I fix the earth clamp on the bracket, right next to the weld, so the current does not pass through bearings, chains or the control panel. I follow the maker's advice to protect any electronics. I weld with screens up to protect others, and a fire watcher with an extinguisher stays during the work and for a set time after. I inspect the weld, refit guards and record the repair.
markingPoints: Isolation permit and hot work permit
Removes or shields burnable items, lines and cables
Checks the material and that the repair is approved
Earth clamp next to the weld; protects bearings and electronics
Screens, fire watch, inspection and record

essays.stem: Explain when a temporary repair is acceptable during a breakdown, and how it must be controlled.
essays.modelAnswer: A temporary repair may be used when the right part or a full repair is not available straight away, and production needs the machine. It is only acceptable if it is safe: it must not remove a guard or safety device, overload any part or make the machine unpredictable. It must be agreed by the person in charge, such as the maintenance supervisor. The repair is marked or tagged on the machine as temporary, and the operator is told of any limits, such as a lower speed or load. It is written in the breakdown report and the maintenance log, with the date by which the permanent repair must be made. The correct part is ordered at once. The temporary repair is checked often until it is replaced. When the permanent repair is done, the record is closed.
markingPoints: Used only when the full repair or part is not available
Must be safe: no guards removed or parts overloaded
Approved by the person in charge
Tagged, limits told to the operator, recorded with a date
Part ordered, checked often, permanent repair closes it

essays.stem: Describe how you would test a machine and hand it back to production after a breakdown repair.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that all tools, rags and loose parts are removed from the machine, and that every guard and safety device is refitted and works. I check fluid levels, belt tension and that bolts are tightened to the torque in the manual. The team is counted and everyone is clear. Each person removes only their own lock, and the authorised person restores the supplies in the right order. I run the machine slowly first, without load, then with a test piece, watching and listening for leaks, noise, heat or vibration. I check the emergency stop works. If there is a problem, I stop and isolate it again. When it runs well, the operator checks the output, such as a test bend. The permit is signed off and returned, and I tell the supervisor it is ready and write the report.
markingPoints: Tools removed; guards and safety devices refitted and working
Levels, tension and torque checked
Team clear; own locks removed; supplies restored
Test run without and with load; emergency stop checked
Operator check, permit signed off, report

essays.stem: Explain what should go in a breakdown report, and how these reports can be used to reduce future breakdowns.
essays.modelAnswer: A breakdown report gives the machine name and number, the date and time it stopped and restarted, and the downtime. It states what the operator saw, the fault found and its root cause. It lists the work done, the parts and materials used, who did the work and any temporary repairs still to be made permanent. It includes any safety issues and recommendations, such as more frequent greasing. Over time, the reports show patterns. The manager can see which machines break down most, which parts fail often and what the downtime costs. Repeat faults can be fixed at the root, for example with better alignment or a stronger part. Planned maintenance can be changed, and spares for parts that often fail can be kept in stores. Operators can be trained where misuse is a cause.
markingPoints: Machine, dates, times and downtime
Fault, root cause and work done
Parts, people, temporary repairs and recommendations
Reports reveal patterns and costs
Used to change planned maintenance, spares and training

essays.stem: As team leader, explain how you would lead a breakdown team of three, including the briefing, sharing tasks, communication with production and safety.
essays.modelAnswer: Before work starts I brief the team on the fault, the permit, the isolations, the hazards and the plan. I check that each person has the right PPE and has fitted a personal lock. I give each person a task that suits their skill: for example, one strips and labels parts, one checks the drive and alignment, and a trainee helps under supervision. Electrical work is left to the licensed electrician. I keep the work area tidy and watch that no one takes short cuts, such as working under a raised ram. I tell the production supervisor the likely repair time and update him if it changes. If we need parts, I arrange them quickly. At the end I make sure everyone is clear before the locks come off, and I lead the test run. I then debrief the team and write the report.
markingPoints: Briefs fault, permit, isolations and hazards
Checks PPE and personal locks
Shares tasks by skill; electrical work to the electrician
Supervises safety and keeps production informed
Controls test run, debrief and report

essays.stem: Compare breakdown maintenance with planned maintenance, and explain how a fabrication shop can reduce breakdowns of its main machines.
essays.modelAnswer: Breakdown maintenance means waiting until a machine fails and then repairing it. It needs little planning, but the failure comes at a bad time, stops production, can damage other parts and may cause injury. Planned maintenance means servicing machines at set times or hours, before they fail. It costs time and parts in advance, but stops are planned and shorter, and machines last longer. A fabrication shop can cut breakdowns by keeping a maintenance plan for each machine from the maker's manual, with daily operator checks such as oil, air and guards, and regular greasing, belt checks and inspections. It should train operators to use machines properly and report early signs, such as noise or leaks. It should keep spares that often fail, record every breakdown and its root cause, and use the records to improve the plan.
markingPoints: Breakdown maintenance explained with drawbacks
Planned maintenance explained with benefits
Maintenance plan from the maker's manual and daily checks
Operator training and early reporting
Spares, records and root-cause improvement

practical1.title: Planned breakdown response on a belt-driven training machine: permit, group lock-off, fault finding and repair
practical1.brief: The assessor has planted two or three mechanical faults on a belt-driven training machine (for example, a pedestal drill or training rig): such as a worn or loose belt, a pulley out of line, a missing key or a dry bearing. The assessor acts as the operator and as the authorised person who issues the permit. Share the roles: team leader, recorder, and two or three fitters. As a group, take the operator's account, then fill in the permit to work with the job, hazards and isolations. The Centre's electrician (or the assessor) isolates and locks off the electrical supply and proves it dead with a tester checked before and after use. Each member fits a personal lock and tag to the hasp. With everyone clear, the start is tried to prove the machine will not start. Find the faults in a logical order, record each one, and put them right using the maker's manual and the right tools (belt tension, pulley alignment with a straight edge, new key, grease). Refit the guards, remove your own locks, and test run the machine with the assessor. Hand back the permit and write a breakdown report. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the permit and report once for the whole group.
materials: Belt-driven training machine with faults planted by the assessor (isolated before work starts)
Permit-to-work forms, multi-lock hasp, a personal padlock and danger tag for each member
Maker's manual or the Centre's maintenance sheet for the machine
Spanners, Allen keys, straight edge, belt tension gauge or rule, grease gun
Spare belt, key and parts as the assessor provides
photos: The completed permit to work, signed by the assessor
The isolator with every member's lock and tag on the hasp
Each fault as it was found, with a label
Pulley alignment or belt tension being checked
The machine with guards refitted, before the test run
checklist: Took part in getting the operator's account and filling in the permit
Fitted a personal lock and tag, and removed only their own lock at the end
Helped prove the machine would not start before work began
Found and recorded at least one fault in a logical order
Put the fault right to the manual, using the right tools
Refitted guards and took part in the test run safely
Contributed to an accurate breakdown report
safety: No work starts until the permit is issued, the supply is locked off and the machine is proved safe
Only the Centre's electrician or the assessor isolates and proves the electrical supply dead
Each person removes only their own lock; guards are refitted before any test run
Keep hands clear of belts and pulleys during the test run; wear safety glasses
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Breakdown weld repair of a broken machine bracket under a hot work permit, with a downtime log and report
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a breakdown on a training conveyor frame or machine mock-up: a guard or support bracket that has broken off and must be repaired. The assessor acts as the production supervisor and as the authorised person. Share the roles: team leader, recorder (keeps a downtime log from the 'breakdown call' to hand-back), fire watcher, and two repair members (the roles change so every member welds or fits part of the repair). As a group, take the account, fill in the permit to work and the hot work permit, and lock off the frame (each member's lock and tag on the hasp). Remove or shield anything that can burn, such as belts, hoses or covers, with welding blankets. Decide whether the bracket is repaired in place or removed, and write a short repair plan: material, joint, electrode and weld size, as the assessor approves. Fix the earth clamp next to the weld, on the bracket. Weld the repair, clean and inspect it, refit the bracket and guard, and test that it is secure. The fire watcher stays during welding and for the time the hot work permit says after. Write a breakdown report with the downtime and a recommendation to stop the bracket breaking again. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the permits, downtime log, plan and report once for the whole group.
materials: Training conveyor frame or mock-up with a broken bracket (set up by the assessor)
Permit-to-work and hot work permit forms; multi-lock hasp, personal locks and tags
MMAW welding machine, electrodes as the plan gives, earth clamp and cables
Welding blankets and screens, fire extinguisher
Grinder, wire brush, clamps, spanners, weld gauge
Downtime log, repair plan sheet and breakdown report form
photos: Both permits filled in, with the locks and tags on the hasp
Burnable parts removed or shielded with blankets
The earth clamp fixed next to the weld on the bracket
The finished weld, cleaned, with a weld gauge on it
The downtime log and the completed breakdown report
checklist: Helped fill in both permits and fitted a personal lock and tag
Removed or shielded burnable parts before hot work
Placed the earth clamp correctly and welded or fitted part of the repair
Inspected the repair and refitted the guard
Kept the fire watch or the downtime log accurately when it was their role
Contributed a sound root-cause recommendation to the report
Worked safely and left the area clean
safety: No hot work until the frame is locked off and the hot work permit is issued
Shield or remove belts, hoses and covers; keep an extinguisher and a fire watcher at hand
Wear full welding PPE; screen the area from other people
Earth clamp next to the weld so current does not pass through bearings or controls
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
